review.notes: Baseline goat/c504700136.lua matches lineage v0 (WC4-003, 2004-02-10) exactly. The whole English lineage is behaviourally unchanged and is not recorded as a change: v0 -> v1 (TP8-EN003, 2006-04-28, 'this monster' -> 'this card') -> v2 (DT05-EN011, 2011-05-29, 'This card gains 500 ATK and DEF. Any monster that destroys this card by battle loses 500 ATK and DEF.') -> v3 (BP01-EN121, 2012-05-24, PSCT 'If this card is destroyed by battle: The monster that destroyed it loses 500 ATK and DEF.', = pinned modern text). The v3 PSCT phrasing is the closest textual correlate of the modern EVENT_BATTLE_DESTROYED timing, but the packet gives no evidence that the BP01 printing is what changed the ruling, so I did not date the ruling change to it - effective is left empty rather than anchored to a printing that only plausibly matches.

event.historical_text: FLIP: Increase the ATK and DEF of this monster by 500 points. The ATK and DEF of a monster that destroys this monster as a result of battle is decreased by 500 points.
event.summary: Era trigger timing, not a text erratum: the goat script fires the ATK/DEF-drain on EVENT_BATTLED gated by s.descon (e:GetHandler():IsBattleDestroyed()), so the mandatory Trigger Effect registers at the end of damage calculation while Slate Warrior is still on the field, whereas the modern script uses EVENT_BATTLE_DESTROYED and so triggers after it has already been sent to the Graveyard. Upstream annotates the variant 'Triggers on the field'. The -500 ATK/DEF applied to the destroying monster and the FLIP +500 are otherwise identical (the remaining diff is RESET_EVENT|RESETS_STANDARD vs the '+' spelling of the same bits). No evidence in the packet dates when the timing changed, so the chronology is unresolved.
